recognize_zh: 骨髓切片中兩顆組織球的細胞質內塞滿數十顆完整的橘紅色紅血球，其中一顆還吞入一個有核細胞，周圍是富含紅血球前驅細胞的骨髓，符合噬血現象（hemophagocytosis）。
features: Two histiocytes distended by numerous intact, orange-red erythrocytes
One histiocyte also contains an engulfed nucleated cell with a dense round nucleus
Histiocyte nuclei inconspicuous, compressed by ingested material
Background cellular marrow with erythroid precursors, occasional larger mononuclear cells and a fat space
Bright eosin staining of red cells (fixative-related)
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy section shows histiocytes containing abundant phagocytosed intact erythrocytes, with one histiocyte also containing a nucleated cell. The surrounding marrow is cellular with numerous erythroid precursors and scattered larger mononuclear cells. No granulomas or overt lymphoma infiltrate is seen in this field. Findings are consistent with hemophagocytosis; in the setting of acute EBV infection, correlation with HLH diagnostic criteria (fever, cytopenias, ferritin, triglycerides, fibrinogen, soluble CD25) is required, as histologic hemophagocytosis alone is neither sensitive nor specific.

ddx.vs: Reactive hemophagocytosis is morphologically identical and is separated from HLH only by clinical and laboratory criteria.
Erythroblastic islands consist of a central macrophage surrounded by, not filled with, maturing nucleated erythroid precursors.
Siderophages contain golden-brown refractile granules that are Prussian blue positive rather than intact round erythrocytes.
Lymphoma-associated cases show an accompanying atypical lymphoid infiltrate highlighted by CD3/CD56/EBER staining.
